svg.aria-label: How one training image becomes queries, in three rows. Annotation: the flower head is one of 7 annotated elements, each with a label, a tight box and a description; face, lips, flower head and stem make queries, while woman, hair and rose name a direction and make none. Query: the box is kept as is a third of the time and otherwise enlarged by 5 to 90 percent, here enlarged; the description is full, its first sentence, 2 to 3 keywords or the label, with shares 25, 30, 35 and 10 percent, here keywords. Moved window: for the first 2 queries, a window of the same size with the same description is moved clear of the related boxes: the element's own box, boxes sharing a concept word, none here, and boxes of the same category, here the rose. Each image gives 6 queries.
svg.text: every element has a label, a tight box b* and a description
name a direction in the description: no query
one per element, 4 elements per image
first 2 queries only; same description, same size as b
boxes sharing a concept word (flower, head): none here
boxes of the same category, flower = {flower, rose}: <rose 1>
Per image: 4 queries, plus 2 moved windows, so 6 queries; a batch of N images gives 6N.
